points.description: States the core advantage: in a doubly-linked list, insertion and deletion can be done in constant time (O(1)), including at positions before a given node/location or at the end of the list (e.g. because each node has a link to its predecessor, or there is direct access to the previous node/tail).
points.partial_credit: 2-3 marks if it says insertion/deletion is easier or faster, or mentions backward/previous-node access, but does not state constant time or the before-a-location/end cases.

points.description: Specifically mentions that operations before a given location or at the end of the list are also constant time (which a singly-linked list cannot do in constant time).
points.partial_credit: 0.5 if only one of the two cases (before a location, or at the end) is mentioned.

rubric.notes: Full marks: says insertion and deletion run in constant time in a doubly-linked list, including before a given node or at the end. Part marks: says insertion/deletion is easier or faster, or that nodes can be traversed both ways or have a previous pointer, without constant time. No marks: answers about unrelated features or only memory use with no link to insertion/deletion.
